newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold to hold above $320.00 support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold to hold above $320.00 support.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Despite downside pressure in New York and Far Eastern markets on Tuesday following testimony to Congress by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Greenspan, gold is expected to hold above support at $320.00 an ounce in European trading on Wednesday.
In fact after initial downside pressure gold has the potential to punch towards $325.00 on short-covering, traders said.

GOLD - After earlier downside pressure following declines in New York and Far Eastern markets overnight gold was unlikely to test support at $320.00 and could possibly mount an attack on $325.00 in later trading on Wednesday, traders said.

New York gold ended lower after U.S. stocks, bonds and the dollar made gains following U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress. He said U.S. economic growth was slowing and that inflation in 1997 was modest, avoiding the need for near-term monetary policy tightening.

"The initial reaction was to move prices lower but when $320.00 never looked like been tested some covering emerged," one trader said. The trader gave a rough trade range of between $$323.00 to just above $325.00 in European trading on Wednesday.
"If we can hold this range then there should be few fireworks around New York's opening," the trader added.

But with gold still reeling from recent 12-year lows after the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tonnes from reserves, several traders suggested that producers might be attempted to sell on any significant gains.
Producer sales from Australia pressured gold in Hong Kong trading overnight.

If $320.00 was breached, prices could fall to a band of support at $318.50/$319.50. Below that there was little to offset a retracement until the 12-year low London gold fix of $315.75 earlier this month.
Overhead resistance was still pegged at $330.00, a level that was unlikely to be tested during the remainder of this week.
At 0758 spot gold was indicated at $323.75/$324.25, against Tuesday's London close of $327.80/$328.30.
SILVER - Seen in narrow ranges. Resistance pegged at $4.40/$4.45, followed by $4.60.
On the downside $4.17 remained key support, a breach of which could see prices driving towards $4.00.
At 0808 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.29/4.31, versus $4.36/38.
PLATINUM - Gains were likely to be limited unless the market could break strong resistance at $420. Support for platinum was seen at $400, followed by $394.
At 0808 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $414.00/417.00, against $417.50/$420.50.
